subject: KiteView trial: deployment path recommendation & logistics
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@kiteview.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@kiteview.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: KiteView trial: deployment path recommendation & logistics

Thanks again for the productive discovery call today — appreciate the clear signal on what success looks like for KiteView. Quick recap and two recommended paths for the trial environment so we can pick and lock dates: 

Summary of your primary goals
- Validate inference latency for instrumented queries at 1k qps (95th <= 350ms)
- Confirm quality parity vs. your in-house rule engine on extraction tasks (F1 target >= 0.86)
- Exercise private data controls (VPC + KMS) for one pilot dataset

Two viable trial deployment options (pros/cons high-level)
1) Hosted trial (fastest onboarding)
   - Time to run: ~2 business days to a working sandbox
   - Pros: no infra on your side, Redwood-managed, streaming enabled, production-like observability
   - Cons: traffic routed through hosted control plane (we provide SOC2 evidence), limited to tenant isolation
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool for you) / short-term reservation
   - Time to run: ~4–7 business days (provision + config)
   - Pros: predictable throughput, model pinning, can simulate higher sustained qps
   - Cons: slightly longer setup, cost commitment for reserve window
3) VPC trial (private control plane, customer VPC peering)
   - Time to run: 7–14 business days depending on networking approvals
   - Pros: meets strict data residency/KMS requirements, closest to Private deployment behavior
   - Cons: requires network ops coordination on your side

Suggested next steps
- You confirm which option you prefer for the trial (Hosted / Dedicated sandbox / VPC trial)
- We schedule a 30–45 minute technical kickoff (Markus + Marissa + your infra lead)
- Redwood delivers a POC runbook and cost estimate (attached: draft runbook + env quote)

If helpful I can surface a recommendation from Markus on the best path given your constraints — I sketched a preference in the attached runbook. Want to lock choice and kickoff Thursday or next Monday?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: kiteview-poc-runbook.pdf (13 pages - draft)
Attachment: env-comparison-quote.xlsx (2 sheets)

From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@kiteview.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@kiteview.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:37:12 -0700
Subject: Re: KiteView trial: deployment path recommendation & logistics

Vanessa — thanks for the concise plan. A few clarifications from our side before we pick a path: 

1) Success criteria we care about (please confirm these map to Redwood monitoring):
   - 95th latency < 350ms for our standard production prompt set (avg token length ~120)
   - End-to-end throughput at 1k sustained qps for 10-minute windows
   - Data controls: ability to bring our KMS and see audit logs for token-level requests

2) On the VPC option: our security team requires mutual TLS for peering and a short checklist (we can share) — do you have a template for the networking playbook?

3) Cost: if we run a 2-week Dedicated sandbox what ballpark should we budget for reserved GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equivalent)? an order-of-magnitude estimate will help us get internal buy-in.

Priya (cc) will join the kickoff and loop in our infra lead once we pick a date. My instinct: start with Hosted to validate latency/quality quickly, then switch a subset to Dedicated for throughput stress testing if hosted looks promising. But open to Markus' recommendation.

—Evan
Evan Morris
Head of Product, KiteView AI
evan.morris@kiteview.ai | +1 (617) 555-0123

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@kiteview.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: KiteView trial: deployment path recommendation & logistics

Evan — thanks for the clear success criteria. Short answers and a recommended path: 

- Monitoring: Redwood can emit latency histograms, token-level traces, and audit logs to your S3 (or push to Splunk/Datadog). We can also hand over a CSV of request-level telemetry at the end of the trial.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM for VPC and Private deployments; hosted can use Redwood-managed KMS but we can enable envelope encryption for customer keys on Dedicated.
- Networking playbook: attaching a short checklist I use for peering and mTLS (see attachment: kiteview-poc-runbook.pdf, appendix B).

Recommendation (sequence):
1) Start with a 72-hour Hosted smoke + functional run (validate latency distribution + quality vs. your golden prompt set). Goal: identify any regression and confirm inference quality (Marissa will run the scoring jobs).
2) If results meet thresholds, spin up a 5-day Dedicated sandbox window (reserved instances) to run sustained throughput at 1k qps with continuous batching enabled. That will prove throughput/cost targets.
3) Parallel prep for a VPC shakeout (network approvals) so we can cut over to a VPC pilot if you need KMS + stricter audit controls for production.

I estimate ballpark cost for a 2-week Dedicated sandbox (A100-class) at ~$25k–$40k depending on region/commit and whether you want preemptible nodes for part of the window. We'll provide a formal quote once you pick exact model size and commitment window.

Proposed immediate dates:
- Hosted smoke: start 2027-06-28 09:00 PT (72 hours)
- Dedicated sandbox: provision start 2027-07-05 (5-day stress window)

Marissa and I will populate the runbook timelines if you confirm.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Attachment: kiteview-poc-runbook.pdf (see Appendix B: Networking checklist)

Thanks — this sequencing makes sense to our security and infra teams. A few operational asks: 

- Can you include a pre-filled network change request template we can hand to our SREs? (helps shorten approvals).
- For the 72-hour hosted smoke, do you limit request volume per API key or should we throttle client-side? we'll run a batch job that simulates production traffic shape.

We'll confirm resource owners on our side after we get your network checklist. Happy to lock the 28th for Hosted smoke if Redwood can commit to a kickoff on the 27th for a 30–45 min tech sync.

—Priya

- Hosted smoke start: 2027-06-28 09:00 PT (kickoff tech sync 2027-06-27 10:00 PT)
